source.title: GRASP: Gated Regression-Aware Skill Proposer for Self-Improving LLM Agents

observations: GRASP proposes ADD/MODIFY/REMOVE skill edits from failed trajectories but does not commit a proposal merely because it was generated.

Each candidate is rerun on a balanced held-out probe against a fresh baseline; it is accepted only for positive net fixes over regressions and no increase in regression count. Rejected candidates leave the library unchanged.

On MedAgentBench with gpt-oss-120b across three seeds, full GRASP reports 88.8% test accuracy. Removing only the acceptance gate while applying every proposed edit unconditionally reports 63.5% at K=4 and 40.1% at K=1, drops of 25.3 and 48.7 percentage points respectively.

Matched-compute variants still run the full probe but discard its verdict and select by proposer preference or randomly, reporting 70.8% and 67.2%, so validation compute alone does not explain the full-gate result.

The paper further reports that adding the same gate to five baseline methods improves each in-domain at K=1, while none improves out of distribution; the authors therefore distinguish the generic value of gating from GRASP's bounded editable-library design.

protocol_inference.claim: A generated candidate memory/skill is not authorized for runtime injection until an independent admission test passes; rejection/no-retention must be a valid state.
protocol_inference.evidence_strength: matched component ablation in a clinical structured-agent benchmark
protocol_inference.canonical_effect: strengthens existing memory_admission_runtime_v1; does not introduce a distinct lifecycle failure and therefore does not justify validator mutation

scope_limits: The benchmark is structured clinical/FHIR agent interaction, not autonomous physical-science laboratory execution.
This does not isolate receiver-side applicability revalidation of an already-retrieved fixed failure record.
The evaluated workflow uses external model execution and benchmark environments; it is not an end-to-end scheduled-Chat zero-external-executor parity mechanism.
